designDecisions: Approvals bind both the policy version string and the snapshot digest, so a decision taken under one requirement set cannot unlock another snapshot with the same version label.
fast skips only checkpoints explicitly marked fastSkippable, all of which already produce DRAFT artifacts; model, valuation, audit, controller and release checkpoints are not relaxable.
A gate decision contains no publish/post/trade/grant field; authority is never widened by an approval.
Stage records exist only to classify interrupted work: on open, any RUNNING stage becomes UNKNOWN_TERMINATED with a reason, so the product never implies an in-place resume.
A review is written to the document before it can satisfy the gate; a failed save rebuilds the gate from the persisted document.
A run is never COMPLETED while a required checkpoint has no stage record; the probe exposed and fixed the weaker earlier rule.

Cordis service proxies cannot dispatch ECMAScript private methods; the service uses module-internal helper names instead (#private threw 'Receiver must be an instance of class FinanceReview' on the first native install).
The separation probe spies on the tool registry and approval service; an approval produced zero calls to register/guard/restrict/execute/request/setPolicy and left the tool-schema hash identical.
Restart evidence comes from a real bundle remove and reinstall, which starts a new financeReview epoch over the same durable domain.
